target_customer: Smartphone users sharing photos (picplz), later iPad and developer audiences
problem: Mobile photo sharing was fragmented across Flickr and Twitter; picplz let phone users take, filter and share pictures to several services.
business_model: Consumer app, no revenue model reported; later paid iPad app and a paid developer platform (App.net per Dealroom)

founders.name: Bryan Berg
founders.background_notes: Named by TechCrunch April 2010 as a former imeem executive behind picplz.

founders.name: Ali Aydar
founders.background_notes: Named by TechCrunch in 2010 as a former imeem executive; ran picplz after the 2011 spin off.

exit.reason: The picplz service shut down on 3 July 2012 and was spun out of the company earlier; no source states what happened to Mixed Media Labs itself, and YC lists it as Inactive.

competitors.name: Flickr
competitors.what: Incumbent photo sharing site that TechCrunch used as a comparison for picplz

technical_complexity.rationale: Mobile capture, filters and multi service posting plus a backend were standard for experienced imeem engineers; scale was the only hard part.

defensibility.rationale: Photo filters and sharing were easy to copy, and Instagram pulled ahead in users within a year without a technical gap between them.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Instagram grew far ahead of picplz by mid 2011 per TechCrunch; picplz was spun off in 2011 and shut down in July 2012.

market_need_then: Smartphone cameras were spreading fast in 2010 and photo sharing from phones was a clear consumer behavior, but picplz focused on a space that Instagram dominated within a year.

branding.name_origin: The picplz product name stands for Pictures, Please (TechCrunch, April 2010). No source explains the corporate name Mixed Media Labs.

rebrands.from: picplz as Mixed Media Labs product
rebrands.to: picplz spun off as an independent company
rebrands.why: PicPlz spun off while Mixed Media Labs prepared a new product (TechCrunch)

branding.community_and_virality: Press coverage by TechCrunch at launch rumor and spin off; no merch or fan communities found.

brand_strength.rationale: picplz was covered by TechCrunch and backed by well known investors, but Instagram's brand outgrew it and the parent company name Mixed Media Labs is generic.

pivots.to: Spin off picplz; Mixed Media Labs builds a broader next product
pivots.why: Instagram pulled far ahead and picplz was reportedly shopped around for cash deals (TechCrunch, 8 July 2011).

outcome_analysis: Mixed Media Labs, founded by former imeem executives, built picplz and raised about $5 million from Andreessen Horowitz in November 2010, but Instagram's growth left picplz behind, so it was spun out in July 2011 and shut down on 3 July 2012. The parent kept working on new products and Dealroom says it later became App.net, but the fate of the YC company itself is not documented in the sources read.
notes: The YC page lists no founders, description or website, and links Crunchbase slug picplz; founders are taken from the TechCrunch April 2010 and July 2011 articles. The $5M November 2010 round is stated by TechCrunch but not labeled with a stage, so it is other. The August 2013 Series B of $1.95M rests on Preqin alone (single database) and conflicts with a search summary of a New York Times line that the company raised $5M; the 2013 date is unverified. A TechCrunch April 2010 article said a16z and others were rumored to have invested already. Dealroom says the company later operated as App.net (single source). Instagram is not in the competitor list because the sources naming it are from July 2011, well after the batch. The tone and logo are unknown.
